title: feat(plugin-audit): a reply in a comment thread notifies the thread's starter and earlier repliers
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMgQGy24aZfzGM8MGSDG7V8)_

repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgT5fpDCjJ7voXxj1ge

Fixes #36074

Part of epic #36062, phase 1 (area b1-CM). Seat claim 7063189874. Flow: dev-thread rule (the card thread builds itself; L1 at L1-a).

## What changes

Before, only an `@mention` notified anyone about a comment. Now a **reply** notifies the thread's starter and the people who replied in it before.

- **How "the people in the thread" is found** (`audit-writers.ts`, `readThreadParticipants`). On a new comment whose `parent_id` is set, the writer follows `parent_id` up to the top-level comment (bounded at 16 hops and cycle-safe; the Console only replies to a top-level comment, so this is one read). The author of each comment on that chain is a participant, and the top-level comment's author is the starter. Then every distinct author of a reply to the top-level comment comes from ONE grouped read, `engine.aggregate('sys_comment', { where: { parent_id: root, thread_id }, groupBy: ['author_id'] })`, i.e. `SELECT author_id … WHERE parent_id = ? AND thread_id = ? GROUP BY author_id` on the existing `parent_id` index. The thread's rows are never read into memory (Prime Directive 5, SQL first). Both reads are held to the reply's own `thread_id` (its record): the walk stops at a parent on another record's thread, and the grouped read carries `thread_id` in its `where`, so a `parent_id` written across records through the API draws nobody from the other thread (L1-a N1). Both reads run in system context: they only produce candidates.
- **Who is skipped.** The reply's author; everyone this reply's `mentions` name, as written and as the mention gate resolved them (they get the mention notice, not two). The mention writer now returns that set, and one `afterInsert` handler (`writeCommentNotices`) runs the mention notice, then the reply notice.
- **Who can see it.** Each remaining candidate passes the mention recipient gate (`admitMentionRecipients`): they must READ the record and this reply, judged in their own envelope (grants, vetted organization claim, the comment read gate). The gate gains one optional input, `notice: 'reply'`, that only changes its log line to `[audit] reply notification withheld`. The reply's author is never told who was withheld (that answer stays the mention's, whose author named the people).
- **What arrives.** A new topic, `collab.reply`, through the same `messaging.emit` ingress (ADR-0030): an inbox notice per reply and person (`dedupKey collab.reply:{replyId}:{uid}`, source = the record, so it opens `/{object}/{id}`), and an e-mail in the mention e-mail's shape (`channels: ['email']`, the comment preview, then the line that opens the record). Payload: `title`, `body` (240-character preview), `actorName`, and `mentionUrl` on the e-mail (the member name is shared so one template shape serves both topics).
- **Titles** in the recipient's language: `messages.repliedToYourComment` ("Bob replied to your comment") for the starter, `messages.repliedInYourThread` ("Bob replied in a comment thread you are in") for the others, `messages.repliedAnonymous` when the reply names no author. Added in all 11 locales of `translations/messages.ts`.
- **E-mail rate.** At most one reply e-mail per person per 10-minute window: the mention e-mail's window under its own key (`replyEmailDedupKey` → `collab.reply.email:{org}:{uid}:{bucket}`; `mentionEmailDedupKey` is byte-identical to before). So **within one window a person can get one mention e-mail plus one reply e-mail**; a reply never holds back a mention e-mail. Inbox notices are not limited, as for mentions.
- **Templates.** `REPLY_EMAIL_TEMPLATES` (the mention templates under `collab.reply`, one per catalog locale), registered by `AuditPlugin` at `kernel:ready` in a call of its own, so one refusal leaves the other.
- **Not notified:** an edit of a reply (`afterUpdate`), a top-level comment, a reply whose parent cannot be found on its own record's thread.
- **Known cost (L1-a N2, not owed here):** each participant is judged by the gate and emitted to one after another inside the reply's write, so a thread with many participants makes posting a reply slower in proportion. The mention writer has the same shape for many mentions.
- **Docs:** `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` (`onMentionsWithheld` names only mentioned users; reply participants the gate withholds are not reported) and `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` (reply bell titles localize to the reader, like mention titles), from the Docs Drift Check's list.
- **The topic pickers offer it** (`service-messaging`, `preference-options.ts`): `collab.reply` joins `PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_TOPICS` beside `collab.mention`, so `GET /api/v1/messaging/preference-options` offers it in the preference and template topic pickers before an organization has stored a reply notice (`preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts` loops over the list). Changeset gains `'@objectstack/service-messaging': patch`.
- Not changed: mention notifications (topic, keys, title, e-mail, gate verdict), comment permissions, notification preferences (none added; a `(collab.reply, email, enabled: false)` or `(*, email)` row mutes the reply e-mail like any topic).

## Why

Card #36074, phase 1 of #36062 (the maintainer agreed to bring reply notifications forward: 「同意」). Someone who started a thread, or replied in it, heard nothing when another person answered.

**Item 3's "which record" in the title:** the card asks the title to say who replied on which record's comment. The title names who replied; the record is reached by opening the notice, exactly like "X mentioned you", which does not name the record either. That clause, like the "earlier repliers" in item 1, was the coordinating seat's own addition, not the maintainer's words. Putting the record's name in the title would need a second, per-recipient field-level read of the record's title field. Seat accepted this reading before the build.

## Verification

- New `comment-reply-notice.integration.test.ts` (10 cases; real ObjectQL over SQLite, so the grouped read runs as SQL; real `MessagingServicePlugin` with outbox, dispatcher, preference filter and template tier): Alice comments, Bob replies → Alice one inbox notice + one e-mail ("Bob replied to your comment", preview, absolute record link), Bob nothing; Bob then Carol → Alice and Bob one each, Carol none, Bob's title "replied in a comment thread you are in"; a reply mentioning Alice → only the mention notice; zh-CN reader → zh-CN subject and link line; three replies in one window → three inbox notices, one e-mail; a reply e-mail and a mention e-mail in one window both send; `(collab.reply, email)` muted → inbox only; a top-level comment and an edit of a reply notify nobody; a reply to a reply walks up to the starter and reaches everyone up the chain and every replier; a reply whose `parent_id` names a comment on another record notifies nobody from that thread (fails with the `thread_id` bound removed).
- `mention-recipient-gate.integration.test.ts` (real kernel, AuditPlugin, real gate) gains 3 cases: the participant who reads the record and the reply is notified while the other organization's user and the one without comment read are withheld; a starter whose record became unreadable gets nothing; the withheld line says `reply`.
- `mention-email.test.ts`: reply templates equal the mention templates under `collab.reply` in every catalog locale; the reply key shape and window; the plugin registers both template sets; a refused registration warns once for each.
- `@objectstack/plugin-audit` full suite: 105 files, 1746 passed (at c83ad1dc); after the N1 and topic-list commits the reply, gate and mention-email files re-run green (4 files, 56 passed), and `service-messaging` `preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts` 9 passed; typecheck clean for both packages. `pnpm typecheck` (src, scripts, test layer): clean. eslint on the 8 touched source files: clean.
- `overlap-check.mjs` before each push: clean against main (no open PR shares these files yet; #36071 edits the same plugin in parallel, the second to land merges main).

Clause-②: yes (widening) — `@objectstack/plugin-audit` emits a new notification topic, `collab.reply` (inbox and e-mail), and loads three new `messages.*` keys (`repliedToYourComment`, `repliedInYourThread`, `repliedAnonymous`) in all eleven locales into the host i18n service; `@objectstack/service-messaging` offers `collab.reply` in its platform topic list; nothing removed or refused
Metadata-protocol: none

Clause-② re-read on the final diff: `yes (widening)`, by CONTRIBUTING.md Human Minimum 5 ("widen … what a published package … exposes") and the precedent of new translation keys declared as widening. No spec, protocol, SDK or door request/response shape changes. The new topic is registered where the platform lists its fixed topics, `PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_TOPICS` in `service-messaging` (declaration L2 7063833407 ① 7); the `mention-email.ts` constants are package-internal (not exported from `index.ts`). Both packages ship `patch` (a non-protocol widening).

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (not touched)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; eslint on the touched files is clean (the full `pnpm lint` is left to CI).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (not touched)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
